content.title: Effect shape
A real external connection
Why cleanup matters
content.text:
Without cleanup, removing the component could leave the timer running.

Then an interface that looks gone could still have code firing in the background.

The cleanup is the instruction that reverses or stops the synchronization started by the Effect.

content.title: Effect or event?
content.text:
A user clicks a “Start connection” button. The click chooses to begin the connection. The Effect can then own the ongoing synchronization with the external system.

This division is useful:

**event handler = user intent**

**Effect = keep an external system synchronized with current React values**

content.question: Which scenario most clearly calls for an Effect?

options.text: Deciding what to do when a button is clicked
Starting and cleaning up a timer that must exist while the component is active
Choosing which color to render from a state value

feedback.correct: The timer lives outside React's render calculation, so synchronization and cleanup are needed.
feedback.incorrect: The timer lives outside React's render calculation, so synchronization and cleanup are needed.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** An Effect is an escape hatch for synchronization with something outside React.
**Senior habit:** State is not a signal that “something must happen.” First identify the external system, then make the smallest synchronization Effect that keeps it aligned.
nextSteps: Write one Effect that synchronizes an external browser property and one Effect that starts and cleans up a timer.
